claims.text: Three current repository source notes preserve the K-group linked-list reversal problem, one explicitly naming LC25; language/API and detailed tail/error contracts are not raw-source facts.
Java ListNode API, complete-group reversal with incomplete tail preserved, no value mutation, and k<1 rejection are explicit answer-side choices used to make the candidate executable and testable.
The iterative complete-group boundary algorithm matches writer and independent reviewer identity-order oracles while preserving node identities and values and producing no cycles.

findings: All three current raw repository sources preserve the K-group linked-list reversal problem, and one explicitly names LC25; none of the raw notes preserves a programming-language API or a detailed incomplete-tail/invalid-k contract.
The candidate keeps those missing details explicit as answer-side executable-contract choices instead of presenting them as recovered source facts.

The iterative implementation uses a read-only kth-node preflight before pointer mutation, freezes groupNext as the half-open right boundary, and reconnects each reversed complete group without crossing into the next group.
Reviewer-extracted Java compiles with warnings as errors and matches a reviewer-owned identity-order oracle across every n=0..100 and k=1..25, plus whole-list and k>n edges.
Independent checks preserve the exact input node identity set and node values, detect cycles, and verify declared k<1 rejection.
The O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims are consistent with the iterative pointer implementation; no fabricated project experience or unresolved source variant was found.
